name: ABRACADABRA
full_name: A Broadband/Resonant Approach to Cosmic Axion Detection with an Amplifying B-field Ring Apparatus
summary: A toroidal-magnet experiment for sub-microelectronvolt axions; ABRACADABRA-10cm is a small prototype that has produced search results.
detection_principle: An axion background generates an effective alternating current in a toroidal static field; a pickup loop and SQUID measure oscillating flux in the nominally near-zero-field center.

status.label: Prototype experiments / R&D
status.evidence: 2021 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: The search for low-mass axion dark matter with ABRACADABRA-10cm

collaboration.name: ABRACADABRA Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No significant signal; the best 95% upper limit reaches 3.2×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
